2	layout: default
3	title : "Setoid.Varieties.Properties module (The Agda Universal Algebra Library)"
4	date : "2021-09-24"
5	author: "agda-algebras development team"
6	---
7	
8	### Properties of the models relation for setoid algebras
9	
10	We prove some closure and invariance properties of the relation `⊧`.  In particular, we prove the following facts (which are needed, for example, in the proof the Birkhoff HSP Theorem).
11	
12	* [Algebraic invariance](#algebraic-invariance). `⊧` is an *algebraic invariant* (stable under isomorphism).
13	
14	* [Subalgebraic invariance](#subalgebraic-invariance). Identities modeled by a class of algebras are also modeled by all subalgebras of algebras in the class.
15	
16	* [Product invariance](#product-invariance). Identities modeled by a class of algebras are also modeled by all products of algebras in the class.
17	
18	
19

59	
60	#### Algebraic invariance of ⊧ {#algebraic-invariance}
61	
62	The binary relation ⊧ would be practically useless if it were not an *algebraic invariant* (i.e., invariant under isomorphism).
63	
64	
65	```agda
66	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}(𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ)(p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) where
67	  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₁ )
68	  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₂ )
69	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans )
70	  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑩)
71	
72	  ⊧-I-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ≅ 𝑩  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
73	  ⊧-I-invar Apq (mkiso fh gh f∼g g∼f) ρ = trans i $ trans ii $ trans iii $ trans iv v
74	    where
75	    -- TODO: refactor this proof using new relational reasoning syntax/style
76	    f = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ fh) ; g = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ gh)
77	
78	    i : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ ≈ ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
79	    i = sym $ cong ⟦ p ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)
80	
81	    ii : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
82	    ii = sym $ comm-hom-term fh p (g ∘ ρ)
83	
84	    iii : f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
85	    iii = cong (proj₁ fh) $ Apq (g ∘ ρ)
86	
87	    iv : f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
88	    iv = comm-hom-term fh q (g ∘ ρ)
89	
90	    v : ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ
91	    v = cong ⟦ q ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)
92	```
93	
94	
95	As the proof makes clear, we show `𝑩 ⊧ p ≈ q` by showing that `𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ ≡ 𝑩 ⟦ q ⟧`
96	holds *extensionally*, that is, `∀ x, 𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ x ≡ 𝑩 ⟦q ⟧ x`.
97	
98	#### Lift-invariance of ⊧ {#lift-invariance}
99	The ⊧ relation is also invariant under the algebraic lift and lower operations.
100	
101	
102	```agda
103	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} where
104	
105	  ⊧-Lift-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
106	  ⊧-Lift-invar p q Apq = ⊧-I-invar (Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 _) p q Apq Lift-≅ˡ
107	
108	  ⊧-lower-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
109	  ⊧-lower-invar p q lApq = ⊧-I-invar 𝑨 p q lApq (≅-sym Lift-≅ˡ)
110	```
111	
112	
113	#### Homomorphic invariance of ⊧
114	Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every homomorphic image
115	of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.
116	
117	
118	```agda
119	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X} where
120	
121	  ⊧-H-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → 𝑩 IsHomImageOf 𝑨 → 𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
122	  ⊧-H-invar Apq (φh , φE) ρ =
123	   begin
124	        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ≈˘⟨  cong ⟦ p ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
125	        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈˘⟨  comm-hom-term φh p (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
126	    φ(  ⟦ p ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   cong (proj₁ φh) (Apq (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ))         ⟩
127	    φ(  ⟦ q ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   comm-hom-term φh q (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
128	        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈⟨   cong ⟦ q ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
129	        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ∎
130	    where
131	    φ⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑩 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑨 ]
132	    φ⁻¹ = SurjInv (proj₁ φh) φE
133	    φ = (_⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ φh))
134	    open Environment 𝑨  using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧ᴬ)
135	    open Environment 𝑩  using ( ⟦_⟧ )
136	    open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]
137	```

141	#### Subalgebraic invariance of ⊧ {#subalgebraic-invariance}
142	Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every subalgebra of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.
143	
144	
145	```agda
146	module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} where
147	  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₁ )
148	  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₂ )
149	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑨)  using ( _≈_ )
150	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using () renaming ( _≈_ to _≈₂_ )
151	  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑨)
152	
153	  ⊧-S-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) →  𝑩 ≤ 𝑨  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
154	  ⊧-S-invar Apq B≤A b = goal
155	    where
156	    hh : hom 𝑩 𝑨
157	    hh = (proj₁ B≤A)
158	    h = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ hh)
159	    ξ : ∀ b → h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b) ≈ h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)
160	    ξ b = begin
161	           h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ≈⟨ comm-hom-term hh p b ⟩
162	           ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈⟨ Apq (h ∘ b) ⟩
163	           ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈˘⟨ comm-hom-term hh q b ⟩
164	           h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ∎
